source.title: EMDR therapy for misophonia: a pilot study of case series
source.source_type: primary uncontrolled pilot case series with pre/post assessment
source.design: single-center uncontrolled prospective pilot case series; 10 baseline participants, 8 treated with EMDR, 7 post-treatment completers

extraction_metadata.scope_note: Primary study methods, participant flow, outcomes, patient-level Table 4 data, safety, limitations, and disclosures were atomized. Background claims from cited literature and bibliography entries were not treated as primary-study atoms.

atoms.canonical_statement: The pilot study aimed to identify misophonia-related disturbing experiences and assess the feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of EMDR for reducing misophonia symptoms and improving mental functioning and quality of life.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This pilot study aimed first to identify relevant experiences related to misophonia symptoms

atoms.canonical_statement: The study was conducted at the outpatient psychiatry clinic of Amsterdam UMC, location AMC, with written informed consent and medical ethics approval.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The study site was the outpatient clinic of the department of psychiatry

atoms.canonical_statement: Fourteen patients were selected from September 2015 to July 2017; six waiting-list patients and four prior CBT nonresponders entered baseline evaluation, for 10 baseline participants.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A total of 14 patients were selected from September 2015 to July 2017

atoms.canonical_statement: Inclusion required a diagnosis of misophonia and age 18 to 65 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Inclusion criteria were diagnosis of misophonia and aged between 18 and 65 years.

atoms.canonical_statement: Exclusion criteria included prior EMDR for misophonia, selected primary psychiatric disorders, recent substance-related disorder, recent structural CNS disorder or stroke, benzodiazepine or stimulant use, suicide risk, and language barriers or illiteracy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Exclusion criteria were: previous EMDR treatment for misophonia

population.label: Eligible patients
exclusion_criteria: Depression or anxiety disorder as primary diagnosis
Structural CNS disorder or stroke within last year

atoms.canonical_statement: The 10 baseline participants were 9 women and 1 man, with mean age 35 years and SD 14.53 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A total of 10 patients (9 [90%] female; mean [SD] age, 35 [14,53] years)

population.label: Baseline sample; 90% female; mean age 35 years (SD 14.53)

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean age at misophonia onset was 13.10 years with SD 9.75 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Mean (SD) age of onset was 13.10 (9.75).

population.label: Baseline sample; mean age at onset 13.10 years (SD 9.75)

atoms.canonical_statement: Five of 10 participants had an Axis I comorbidity, none had comorbid PTSD, and Axis II personality traits were reported in 6 of 10.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Fifty percent of the patients fulfiled criteria

population.label: Baseline sample; Axis I comorbidity 50%; PTSD 0%; Axis II traits 60%

atoms.canonical_statement: The baseline sample combined 6 patients from the CBT waiting list and 4 previous CBT nonresponders.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: patients on the waiting list for G-CBT (n = 6) and non-responders to G-CBT (n = 4) were included.

population.label: Baseline sample: 6 CBT waiting-list patients and 4 CBT nonresponders

atoms.canonical_statement: Misophonia-related disturbing memories were identified in 8 of 10 baseline participants; those 8 received EMDR. Seven completed post-treatment assessment and one dropped out after the first session.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In eight of the 10 patients, misophonia-related emotionally disturbing memories were identified

atoms.canonical_statement: EMDR used the standard eight-phase protocol and focused on misophonia-related emotionally disturbing memories identified through a standardized time-line search strategy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The EMDR therapy was conducted according to the standard eight-phase protocol

concept.text: Eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy

exposures.details: Standard eight-phase EMDR protocol focused on misophonia-related emotionally disturbing memories.

atoms.canonical_statement: Target memories were ordered from events linked to symptom onset to later events linked to symptom worsening; each target received a SUD rating before processing.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The order of targets was set; starting with targets that were related to the onset

atoms.canonical_statement: Each EMDR session lasted 60 to 90 minutes; treatment ended when the SUD score was zero for all indexed misophonia-related memories.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each EMDR session lasted 60–90 minutes.

concept.text: Eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy

exposures.details: Standard eight-phase EMDR protocol focused on misophonia-related emotionally disturbing memories.

atoms.canonical_statement: Among seven treatment completers, the mean number of EMDR sessions was 2.6; Table 4 shows a range of 1 to 4 sessions among treated participants.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On average, 2.6 sessions of EMDR were provided to each participant (n = 7).

concept.text: Eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy

exposures.details: Standard eight-phase EMDR protocol focused on misophonia-related emotionally disturbing memories.

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary self-reported outcome was AMISOS-R, a 10-item misophonia symptom scale scored from 0 to 40, with higher scores indicating greater severity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Misophonia symptoms were measured using the revised Amsterdam Misophonia Scale

concept.text: AMISOS-R total score

outcome.definition: 10-item scale scored 0 to 40; higher scores indicate more severe misophonia

atoms.canonical_statement: The co-primary outcome was CGI-I, rated by an independent assessor from 1, very much improved, to 7, very much worse.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The co-primary outcome was CGI-Improvement (CGI-I)

concept.text: Clinical Global Impression Improvement scale (CGI-I)

atoms.canonical_statement: Full response required at least 25% AMISOS-R reduction and CGI-I below 3; partial response required either criterion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Full response was defined by 25% reduction (or more) in the AMISOS-R

concept.text: Treatment response classification

outcome.definition: Full response: >=25% AMISOS-R reduction and CGI-I <3; partial response: either criterion

atoms.canonical_statement: Secondary outcomes were SCL-90-R total score for general psychopathology and the Sheehan Disability Scale for work, social, and family disability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: General mental dysfunction was assessed with the Symptom Checklist-90-R

concept.text: Secondary mental health and disability outcomes

outcome.definition: SCL-90-R total and SDS work/social/family domains

atoms.canonical_statement: SUD was used to rate distress for identified target memories from 0 to 10 before, during, and after EMDR.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Participants were requested to indicate the SUD score verbally to the therapist

concept.text: Subjective Units of Distress (SUD)

atoms.canonical_statement: The Impact of Events Scale was administered only when posttraumatic stress symptoms were suspected and was not a prespecified study outcome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The severity of posttraumatic stress symptoms was measured on indication

concept.text: Impact of Events Scale (IES)

outcome.definition: Conditional measure for suspected posttraumatic stress symptoms

atoms.canonical_statement: The main pre/post analysis used paired two-tailed t-tests with P<.05 as the significance threshold, and the authors described all analyses as exploratory.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All results should be considered as exploratory.

atoms.canonical_statement: An intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis included all participants who received EMDR and imputed missing values by last observation carried forward.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Missing values were hereby imputed by the last observation carried forward (LOCF).

atoms.canonical_statement: No formal sample-size calculation was performed because the study was a pilot.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Since this is a pilot study no formal sample size calculations were performed.

atoms.canonical_statement: Among seven completers, mean AMISOS-R fell from 30.43 to 24.29; the reported mean change was -6.14 points with SD 5.34 and P=.023.

atoms.canonical_statement: The safety section states that no adverse events were reported while also documenting treatment-emergent suicidal ideation and other side effects; the paper does not explain the event-classification boundary.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: No adverse events were reported.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that EMDR focused on emotionally disturbing misophonia-related memories may reduce misophonia symptoms, but larger randomized trials are needed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the results of this study suggest that EMDR therapy is a promising and time-limited intervention

atoms.canonical_statement: The case series had no control group, preventing separation of treatment effects from time effects and nonspecific factors.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The lack of a control group prevents us from assessing the effects of time and of non-specific factors

atoms.canonical_statement: The small sample limits generalizability and prevented meaningful predictor, post-hoc, or comparative-efficacy analyses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The small sample warrants caution in the generalization of the results.

atoms.canonical_statement: There was no follow-up assessment because waiting-list participants proceeded to CBT after EMDR, so durability of response could not be assessed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: There was no follow-up assessment since half of the patients were on the waiting list for CBT

atoms.canonical_statement: The sample combined CBT waiting-list patients and prior CBT nonresponders, creating two subpopulations in a very small cohort.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The inclusion of two subpopulations can be considered a limitation in this small sample.

atoms.canonical_statement: All EMDR was delivered by one therapist, the outcome evaluator was not blind to treatment, and treatment-fidelity measures were not collected.
